judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals carry visible mechanical defects — the party defined as ENET is written "(“SENET”)" and the date reads "the a4. day of February 1995" — and the recital that ENET "owns and operates the sole wireless cable system" is a factual assertion of uncertain effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The last ENET recital conditions the exchange on issuance of a license relocating the D Group Station to Bethesda, whereas the operative Section I.A starts the term on the date of signature and Section II.D allocates the risk of denial, so recital and operative text pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and a fixed expiry date (August 29, 1998) leave nothing to construe on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with Section I.B's automatic renewal running to ten years from the date hereof, though Section VIII.B's reference to "the last automatic renewal term" hints at more renewals than I.B provides.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing "unless ENET provides ... notice" is syntactically detached from the renewal condition, and "Provided that ... the University shall have filed an application for renewal" makes renewal turn on an act the University elsewhere may decline; the singular "an additional term" is also in tension with the notion of successive renewals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections I.C.1, VIII.B and XIII.A all speak of "the last automatic renewal term under Section I.B" as though several renewals exist, while VIII.B lets the University elect not to renew the License at all — a genuine incoherence with this clause's renewal condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "during any or all of the period" and "exclusive right to match" are loosely drawn, leaving unclear whether the right attaches to offers made during, or leases commencing during, the two-year window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with I.C.2 and I.C.3, whose notice mechanics (commencement of negotiations vs. seven days after a bona fide offer) do not line up cleanly with this grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause requires notice "at the commencement of any negotiations" and then in the next sentence that "[s]uch notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — two incompatible timing rules for the same notice, and "the contract" is itself ambiguous as between this Agreement and the proposed lease.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Set against I.C.1 and I.C.3, which fix the ROFR window by reference to expiration of the automatic renewal term, the one-year rule cannot be harmonised with a notice triggered by the start of negotiations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "bona fide offer ... acceptable to the University" and matching "on substantially the same material terms" are elastic standards, and the anti-frustration sentence ("purpose or the effect of preventing") is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the ROFR scheme in I.C.1 and I.C.4 but inherits I.C.2's conflicting one-year notice requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward re-run of the ROFR procedure on any materially changed offer; "material term" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with I.C.1 through I.C.3, which it expressly incorporates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses the collective term "FCC Applications" before it is defined (in II.A.2) and leaves "such other changes ... as ENET believes necessary" to ENET's unilateral belief.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The PTP Link is described as running to the "Leesburg campus" while Schedule B lists the GWU Northern Virginia campus at Ashburn, a minor mismatch with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "quality and reliability at least equal to RS 250B" and the trigger "if the parties are unable to reach agreement after good faith negotiations" are both indeterminate, and the refund is of the Commitment Fee "less the University's reasonable costs" without a cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly with II.D.1 (University "shall retain the commitment fee") and with XIII.N's $15,000 cap on reimbursable negotiation costs, which points the other way on the same money.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains the mechanical slip "ECC Applications" for "FCC Applications" and the odd standard "at such time as ENET reasonably determines to be provident."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its $15,000 fee-sharing machinery says ENET "may notify" the University, whereas the parallel provision in XIII.A says ENET "shall notify" — the same mechanism stated two different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical list is introduced by "including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing," and "best efforts" plus "reasonable requirements of ENET" leave the obligation's boundary open; the proviso making costs payable only if "approved by ENET in advance" makes ENET's own cost obligation self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates III.E.1 almost verbatim for modifications, and its cost-approval proviso must be read against XIII.N's broad reimbursement obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause calls the instrument "this Service Agreement" — a name used nowhere else — and refers to "the commitment fee" in lower case with a cross-reference to Paragraph V.A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lets the University retain the whole Commitment Fee on denial, while II.A.2 requires a refund of that fee (less costs) on a different failure route, and the cross-reference to "best efforts pursuant to Paragraph XII.A" points to a filings clause rather than II.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "best efforts to seek an alternative transmission source" and "cannot be utilized" are soft, but the termination mechanics and ten-day window are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels II.E.2 and the cross-reference to "Paragraph XII.A" (rather than II.B) is the sort of slip that recurs through Section II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite termination right on a defined trigger; "conditions materially adverse" is the only judgment term and is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with II.D.1, II.E.2 and Section XI's termination scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rescission mechanism is clear enough, though "materially adverse to ENET" is a judgment standard and the excusal of ENET's STL/PTP obligations is stated without detail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks II.D.2's structure and does not appear to collide with Section XI or III.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sequence is incoherent on its face: the University "may terminate" and only then may ENET offer an indemnity, with no statement of what happens to the already-effected termination if the offer is accepted; "reasonable discretion" compounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere (Section XI, IX.A) explains the effect of an accepted indemnity offer on a termination already given, leaving the scheme unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering" is broad but the sentence itself is clear in placing them on ENET.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N caps reimbursable negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000 while this clause makes ENET bear all such costs of "the preparation of this Agreement" without limit — a specific conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains "until the date that is ten years from the date hereon" (for "hereof"), leaves "state-of-the-art equipment" and "then-current market value of such used equipment" undefined, and draws an unexplained line between shared and non-shared equipment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties the purchase option to "nonrenewal ... for reasons other than the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)", but XI.B(2) is a termination right for the University's breach, not a nonrenewal right, and I.B gives ENET the non-renewal notice — a mismatch across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs reorientation of antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", but Schedule A is the programming list; the receive sites are on Schedule B — a mechanical error that changes what is required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: X.B.5 expressly warrants that "Schedule B accurately identifies the site and receive antenna", confirming the cross-reference here is wrong and the two provisions cannot both be right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends mid-thought — "and begun broadcasting the D Group" — leaving the final condition of the Start Date incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.C fixes the first Royalty by reference to when the Station "has been constructed and is broadcasting" rather than to the defined Start Date, so two different triggers exist for essentially the same event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "technical direction, supervision and control of the University" alongside ENET's operational duty, and "continuous feed" with its parenthetical gloss, leave some room but the allocation is largely explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENET's promise to bear "all costs and expenses associated with operating and maintaining" sits against XIII.N, under which ENET reimburses the University for costs of "operating and maintaining the D Group Station" — overlapping and potentially double-counting obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same open-ended construction as II.C.1: "best efforts", "reasonable requirements of ENET" and an illustrative list preceded by "without limiting the generality of the foregoing".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It nearly duplicates II.C.1, and Section IV's carve-out refers to "Paragraphs III-E.1 or III.E.2" as affecting capacity allocation, which this clause does not address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a compound of vague conditions ("reliable and cost-effective", "no material degradation in quality"), and the emergency carve-out permitting verbal approval by "an executive of ENET" undercuts the written-approval rule in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This paragraph addresses digital compression only "on channel D1", yet Section IV says implementation of digital technology pursuant to III.E.1 or III.E.2 affects recapture capacity on channels D3 and D4 — the two cannot be squared.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short negative covenant with a familiar "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier; little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bars the University from amending the FCC Applications without ENET's consent, while II.C.1 obliges the University to amend at ENET's request and XII.A subjects every filing to the University's consent — three consent rules that must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term is mis-typed as "(SENET Capacity)", the grant is for "any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information", and "All capacity that is not ENET Capacity shall be deemed University Capacity" is stated absolutely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII forbids ENET from transmitting anything outside an approved list without University consent, flatly contradicting the unrestricted-use grant here; and the residual "University Capacity" definition ignores Hybrid's rights on D2 recognised in XIII.Q and the D2 option in XIII.M.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sum payable on execution; nothing ambiguous in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fate on early termination is dealt with inconsistently elsewhere (II.A.2 refund less costs vs. II.D.1 retention), though the clause itself is neutral on that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is broken — "the greater of: Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) or (ii) Twenty Cents ($0.20) for each subscriber" omits "(i)" — and "for each subscriber" leaves open whether the comparison is per subscriber aggregate or per subscriber unit, and which service's subscribers count.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.M's parallel D2 royalty uses the same greater-of formula at ten cents, and V.B.1's subscriber count rules must be read into this clause; the definitional gap in "subscriber to ENET's wireless cable service" runs across both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula is garbled — "by dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by ENET's then prevailing monthly rate" — a duplicated operator in the operative calculation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the count used by V.B and V.C and does not appear to contradict any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "on twentieth day of each subsequent month" drops the article, and the certificate must show subscribers "served during each month of such period" though the royalty is computed on a first-day-of-month headcount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The first-payment trigger here (Station constructed and broadcasting) differs from the defined Start Date in III.C, which also requires the STL and PTP Links and the Modification Plan — two different commencement points for the same payment stream.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The eighteen-month retention period and the once-a-year audit right are stated definitely; "at any time or times ... during reasonable business hours" is only mildly loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The thirty-business-day notice and the ninety-day post-service window fit the royalty provisions in V.B and V.C without evident conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "shall not interfere with the right of ENET to lawfully modify, waive, rescind, terminate or cancel" is a definite list with a plain effect on unperformed contracts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the $2,500 monthly floor in V.B, which protects the University against subscriber attrition, so no real inconsistency appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence proration rule with a plain arithmetic effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to whatever termination route Section XI or II.D/II.E produces and does not conflict with the minimum-royalty structure in V.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Placing all applicable taxes and fees other than income taxes on the University is unusual but stated clearly; "fees" is the only elastic word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with XIII.N's reimbursement obligation, under which ENET pays the University's costs of complying with the Agreement — arguably including such fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The standard is doubly vague — "of the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations ... in such amounts as are customarily carried under similar circumstances" — and the enumerated policies follow "including, without limitation", the classic general-versus-specific setup.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The specifics in VI.A.1 and VI.A.2 sit beneath this open-ended standard, but nothing elsewhere in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-risk" property insurance at full replacement value is a defined market concept; the wording is short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It insures the D Group Station though III.A contemplates ENET owning the transmission equipment and the University holding only a purchase option, leaving insurable-interest allocation implicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed dollar limits per occurrence, per aggregate and for property damage; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VI.A's chapeau and VI.B's policy-form requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice unallocated, which is the sort of phrase parties argue over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with VI.A and does not collide with the indemnity provisions in Section IX.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted-programming list ends with the garbled catch-all "or an other programming agreed to by the University", and the University's "absolute right" to deny obscene programming sits against a consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld" — a general-versus-specific and mechanical problem together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IV grants ENET its capacity "for any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information", which directly contradicts this approval regime; Schedule A also describes itself as merely "representative types" while this clause treats it as the identified list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all licenses, permits and authorizations required or desired" and "could reasonably be expected to cause the FCC to impair" are broad, though the duties are recognisably best-efforts covenants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to "take all necessary steps to renew" is expressly subject to VIII.B, which permits the University to surrender or not renew the License — a carve-out that swallows much of the covenant and interacts with I.B's renewal condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause runs words together ("willing to assumeall remaining obligations") and grants a surrender right "[d]uring the Term ... or at anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term", a period that may not exist under I.B.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits the University to abandon the very License that VIII.A obliges it to preserve and that I.B makes the condition of renewal, and it duplicates the assignment machinery in XIII.A with different triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limb sweeps in "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" after a list of specific media torts — a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is open — and the sub-clauses are numbered "(1)" then "(ii)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indemnity for obscene or indecent transmissions overlaps the University's approval and denial rights in Section VII, but the two can largely be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mirror-image indemnity with three enumerated triggers and no catch-all; the wording is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is narrower than ENET's indemnity in IX.A, but asymmetry between mutual indemnities is a bargain, not an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" gives the claimant an unbounded veto over the acknowledgment that triggers the procedure, which is a genuine soft spot.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to both IX.A and IX.B and does not contradict the notice provisions in XIII.L.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard organisation representation stated in definite terms, forward-looking as a covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits X.C's survival provision and mirrors X.B.1 for the University.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant to comply with "all laws, rules and regulations governing its business and the ITFS facilities" is unqualified by materiality, but the sentence is otherwise conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel University representation in X.B.2 is qualified "in all material respects", an asymmetry within the same section that a court could be asked to explain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence stating that all requisite resolutions have been adopted; nothing elastic in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.B.3 and is consistent with X.C's survival rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "to ENET's best knowledge" and "does not know of any valid basis" are knowledge qualifiers of familiar type; the repetition of the no-pending-proceedings sentence is redundant rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels X.B.4, except that the University's version adds an adverse-impact qualifier this one lacks — an asymmetry, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "EENET" is a typographical slip and "has reasonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a notably vague financial representation whose content a court would have to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines or supports this assurance, and Section XI gives the University no financial-condition termination right to give it teeth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite organisation and eligibility representation, restated as a continuing covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise to retain eligibility to hold the License sits against VIII.B, which lets the University surrender or not renew that License — a tension worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Qualified "in all material respects", with conventional no-conflict and no-consent language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against XIII.Q, which acknowledges pre-existing obligations to Hybrid that could conflict with performance here — the very thing the no-conflict representation denies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence about corporate authorisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.A.3 and raises no cross-provision issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge qualifiers and the added "which would have an adverse impact on the University's obligations" narrow the representation, but the wording is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with X.A.4's mirror and with X.C's survival and notification duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about a schedule that, as executed, contains entries marked "Omitted" and incomplete coordinates — the warranty is difficult to apply to that document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.B directs antenna reorientation at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", contradicting this provision's premise that Schedule B is the receive-site list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any event or circumstance which might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is a loose trigger for the notification duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It converts representations into continuing covenants, which interacts with the termination rights in XI.A(2) and XI.B(2) for breach of "material obligations" but does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "breaches any of its material obligations" is undefined, and the "either (a) ... or (b)" structure appears to let the University terminate whenever either limb is met even though (b) is the more forgiving cure standard — a drafting slip that changes the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "without further liability to ENET" is hard to reconcile with XI.C, which preserves the terminating party's damages claim, and termination under this paragraph triggers the $1.00 equipment purchase in III.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1)'s carve-out ("unless such termination is due to a breach by ENET") lets ENET terminate on an event it may have caused, limb (3) lets ENET terminate simply by ceasing to serve the market, and "material obligations" is again undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.A denies the University the $1.00 (and even the market-value) purchase right where ENET exercises "its rights under Section XI.B.(2)", a cross-reference that does not match this paragraph's structure cleanly, and XI.C cuts against "without further liability".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is short and clear in preserving damages claims for the terminating party only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XI.A and XI.B each say termination is "without further liability" to the other party, and II.D, II.E likewise; reconciling those with a preserved damages claim is a genuine internal problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The qualifier "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld" is buried mid-sentence so that its object is unclear, and the closing sentence gives the University an apparently unqualified consent right "[n]otwithstanding anything herein to the contrary".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That absolute consent right is difficult to square with II.A.2 (University must file within thirty days or negotiate), II.C.1 (University shall amend on ENET's request) and III.E.3, all of which assume filings the University cannot simply refuse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mixes "best reasonable efforts" and "reasonable best efforts" within a few lines and requires "such reasonable protests" as ENET requests, standards whose content is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to obtain and maintain all licenses overlaps VIII.A and sits against VIII.B's right to surrender the License; the reimbursement proviso overlaps XII.C and XIII.N.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence repeats "incurred by the University" and is otherwise a plain reimbursement covenant limited to Section XII obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside II.F and XIII.N, the latter beginning "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" and capping certain legal and engineering fees at $15,000 — three overlapping cost-allocation clauses with different scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first permits assignment only if the assignee assumes all obligations, then, "[s]ubject to the foregoing provisions", permits assignment to an entity that does not assume them — an internal contradiction in consecutive sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces VIII.B's assignment machinery with different triggers and, unlike II.B's parallel fee provision, says ENET "shall" (not "may") notify the University about $15,000 in fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts language with a plain effectiveness rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement bears on execution formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "It is the intention of the University" is precatory while "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" is an obligation without any measure of the assistance owed — a genuine open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The distance-learning use must fit within "University Capacity" as defined in Section IV and within the recapture windows there, which this clause never addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional merger and written-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals and XIII.Q preserve the earlier Hybrid Agreement, which is with a different party, so the supersession language does not obviously bite on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of executory character with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not cut against any other provision, though its practical function (bankruptcy characterisation) is not developed anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated events end in "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" — a catch-all against specifics inviting ejusdem generis — and "the period of dependency of any such contingency" appears to be an error for pendency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "[N]or shall any charges or payments be made in respect thereof" is hard to reconcile with the $2,500 monthly minimum royalty in V.B and the proration rule in V.F.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "best efforts" plus a sweeping negative covenant not to "take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted" is broad and boundary-less.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That negative covenant is difficult to square with VIII.B and XIII.A, which expressly permit the University to surrender, not renew or assign the License in ways that plainly affect ENET's rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Naming a federal statute, agency rules and District of Columbia law as the governing body of law without a priority rule leaves a small ordering question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with XIII.K's forum provision and XIII.P's reformation clause without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings-for-convenience language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It neutralises the several garbled headings in this document rather than creating any conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause disclaims contra proferentem in clear terms; it is itself definite, though it is precisely the tool a court might otherwise reach for in this heavily one-sided instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies across the Agreement and does not conflict with XIII.T's word-meaning rules or XIII.H's governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "District of Columbia courts" is genuinely ambiguous as between the federal courts sitting in the District and the local D.C. courts, and "any party shall have the right to sue" leaves the clause permissive rather than exclusive despite the irrevocable submission that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the notice provision in XIII.L for service of process, which is consistent, and no other clause addresses forum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed receipt "the first weekday (excluding Federal holidays) after being sent" is definite, and the permitted delivery methods are enumerated exclusively.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception for Royalty payments matches V.C's first-class mail rule, so the two fit; the exclusivity of Express Mail/Federal Express could matter for the many notice deadlines in Sections I, II and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall have the exclusive tight to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" states the option and its exercise mechanics, but says nothing about what happens if ENET does not exercise within twenty-one days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.Q subordinates all ENET rights to Hybrid's D2 rights "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary", and Section IV defines ENET Capacity as D3 and D4 with everything else deemed University Capacity — both pull against this option.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause opens "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein" and then caps only the negotiation fees at $15,000 while leaving "otherwise complying with the terms of this Agreement" uncapped — a general-versus-specific tension in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges ENET to reimburse the University for "operating and maintaining the D Group Station", though III.D makes ENET itself responsible for those costs, and it caps fees that II.F says ENET bears in full.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]either party shall present itself as ... having any relationship with one another, except as set forth under the terms of this Agreement" is oddly absolute and its boundary is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with XIII.C's program-guide listing obligation and Section VII's programming controls, which necessarily involve some public association.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to "promptly negotiate in good faith to reform and amend" with no fallback is a classic open term, and the covenant not to "take any action that contributes to" an adverse regulatory change is very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against XIII.D's written-modification requirement and XIII.P.2's acknowledgement that FCC rules may change the capacity allocation, without saying what happens if negotiation fails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement with no operative obligation; it is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites the same FCC Report and Order as Section IV but dates it July 9, 1994 where Section IV says July 6, 1994, and it subjects the capacity allocation to future rule changes that Section IV states shall not be affected by digital implementation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he obligation of the University to take any action required hereunder shall be read to conform to such other obligations" is an open-ended override, and the proviso barring any action adverse to Hybrid "in the reasonable judgment of the University" gives one party the judgment call.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides everything to the contrary, which directly limits ENET's D2 option in XIII.M and the capacity grant in Section IV, and cuts across the University's affirmative duties in II.C.1, III.E and XII.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, absolute time-of-the-essence rule; clear in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read across the whole instrument it collides with the many soft timing standards — "as soon as reasonably possible" in III.A, "best efforts", "promptly" — and with the automatic extension of all time limits in the force majeure clause XIII.F.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional non-waiver language, though "any other failure in the future or in the past" is awkwardly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the cure-and-notice mechanics in XI.A and XI.B without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "Final Order" definition is carefully drawn in two limbs; "[a]ll pronouns and any variations therefore" contains a small spelling slip that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition is cross-referenced correctly from II.D.1 and is used consistently throughout Sections II, VIII and XIII.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Schedule describes only "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit" and cross-refers to "Subparagraph 3 (C)", a provision that does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as the definitive list of "programming networks identified on Schedule A" that ENET may transmit without consent, while III.B refers to receive sites "listed on Schedule A" — three inconsistent uses of the same schedule.
